spec: draft-zambo-aer1-18 Section 4: producers and verifiers MUST NOT apply Unicode normalization (such as NFC or NFD) to the canonical bytes at any point. Visually identical strings with different UTF-8 byte sequences are different payloads and hash differently, by design. Presenting the NFD bytes against the NFC commitment is a verification failure, not a match.

vectors.desc: The four-character string c, a, f, U+00E9 (LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH ACUTE) in NFC form: five bytes, SHA-256 as stated in draft-zambo-aer1-18 Section 4. The recomputed digest MUST equal the stated commitment.
vectors.name: unicode-nfc-form

vectors.desc: The same visible string in NFD form (c, a, f, U+0065, U+0301 COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT): six bytes, SHA-256 as stated in draft-zambo-aer1-18 Section 4. The recomputed digest MUST equal the stated commitment, and MUST differ from the NFC commitment.
vectors.name: unicode-nfd-form

vectors.desc: The NFD bytes presented against the NFC commitment (the sha256 field carries the NFC digest). The recomputed digest MUST NOT equal the stated commitment: a verifier MUST NOT normalize the payload and then report agreement.
vectors.name: unicode-nfd-against-nfc-commitment
